program.source: export function evaluate({ inputs, time, seed, state }) { const launchSpeed = inputs.launchSpeed; const gravity = 9.8; const t = time; const height = launchSpeed * t - 0.5 * gravity * t * l2(t); const velocity = launchSpeed - gravity * t; const apexTime = launchSpeed / gravity; const apexHeight = (launchSpeed * launchSpeed) / (2 * gravity); const isAtTop = Math.abs(t - apexTime) < 0.05; const motionState = t < apexTime ? "Moving up" : (isAtTop ? "Still for an instant" : "Moving down"); const gravityState = "Gravity pulls down"; const py = 300 - height * 40; const ballObj = sdk.circle("ball.toss", 320, py, 28, { role: "output" }); const vArrow = sdk.vector("vec.v", { x: 320, y: py }, { value: velocity, direction: "up" }, { scale: 15, minLength: 12, label: "v", role: "output" }); const aArrow = sdk.vector("vec.a", { x: 350, y: py }, { value: -gravity, direction: "up" }, { scale: 5, minLength: 12, label: "a", role: "observed" }); const calloutObj = sdk.callout(380, py - 20, [motionState, gravityState], { id: "callout.toss", role: "output" }); const laneObj = sdk.panel({ x: 40, y: 40, w: 560, h: 360, title: "Vertical Toss", state: motionState, id: "lane.toss" }); const axisObj = sdk.axis("axis.height", { x: 80, y: 380, length: 300, orientation: "y", min: 0, max: 3, label: "Height", unit: "m" }); const guideObj = sdk.groundMark("ground.guide", 320, 380, 80, "Launch"); return { frame: { width: 640, height: 420, objects: [laneObj, axisObj, guideObj, ballObj, vArrow, aArrow, calloutObj], readouts: [{ id: "motionState", value: motionState }, { id: "gravityState", value: gravityState }] }, quantities: { launchSpeed, gravity, apexTime, apexHeight, velocity, height } }; function l2(t) { return t * t; } }

manifest.title: The ball stops rising. Gravity doesn’t stop.
manifest.summary: Gravity slows the ball on the way up and speeds it up on the way down. At the top, the ball is still for an instant while gravity pulls downward.
manifest.description: A ball moves vertically on a height scale. A blue vector shows its velocity, shortening as it rises and pointing downward as it falls. A dashed warm vector indicates constant downward acceleration due to gravity.
manifest.instructions: Change launch speed, then press Play. At the top, playback pauses so you can inspect the arrows.
